climbing_route.label: South Slope
climbing_route.notes: Above the waterfalls the gully opens into brush, forest, and then heather meadows/slopes — the 'South Slope' — which are followed up toward the East Ridge.

climbing_route.label: East Ridge to the summit
climbing_route.notes: A final ~300 feet of solid, enjoyable Class 3 scrambling on the East Ridge to the 6,113 ft summit.

climbing_route.label: West ridge crest to the col
climbing_route.notes: From the 6,700-6,800 ft shoulder, work up the ridge crest — some class 4 moves getting established — to gentler but loose, cairned terrain leading to a col with a good bivy site.

climbing_route.label: First gully on the southwest/west ridge
climbing_route.notes: From the col, cross talus to the base of the first obvious gully leading up the southwest/west ridge: steep class 3/4 at its bottom, then broadening and easing after a string of cairns; follow it to the ridge crest. Terrain here is loose and unmarked.

climbing_route.label: Ridgecrest to the summit
climbing_route.notes: The exposed but moderate ridgecrest leads to the summit.

climbing_route.label: South ridge from the 7,800-ft notch
climbing_route.notes: A rising traverse across a talus bowl gains a key 7,800-ft notch on Arriva's south ridge; from the notch a final scramble leads to the summit. The source text describes nothing further about this ground.

climbing_route.label: Coleman and Deming Glaciers
climbing_route.notes: From Hogsback Camp, rope up on the Coleman and Deming Glaciers — crevasses and route-finding.

climbing_route.label: Roman Wall
climbing_route.notes: The crux: steep snow at roughly 40 degrees between the Deming Glacier and the summit plateau.

wa_mount_baker_coleman_headwall.skip_reason: The approach text ends at the base of the headwall near 8,500 ft and describes no climbing above it. The only headwall content is timing/hazard advice (the headwall and the Black Buttes shed rock and ice as the day warms, so parties leave camp 11 p.m.-4:30 a.m. to be past the glacier crossing and lower headwall before the sun hits it), with no line, feature or grade for the 14 pitches.

climbing_route.label: Double bergschrund start
climbing_route.notes: The base of the North Ridge proper is on the Coleman Glacier's true right side. The standard start crosses a double bergschrund via a bridge or narrow snow ramp — can be a difficult, exposed step depending on the season, and can close out entirely by late summer.

climbing_route.label: Snow gully to the ridge crest
climbing_route.notes: Climbs a broad 40-degree snow gully to the crest of the ridge. The route sees far less traffic than Coleman-Deming, so tracks and bridges may be unbroken.

climbing_route.label: South/southeast talus slopes
climbing_route.notes: From a Shellrock Basin or Eureka Creek camp, gain the Carru-Osceola col or Rolo Pass and scramble the south/southeast talus slopes to the summit ridge.

climbing_route.label: Left-to-right diagonal ramp, west face
climbing_route.notes: At the base of Chaval's broad west face the ascent line's obvious left-to-right diagonal ramp begins. The gullies just below the west face are avalanche terrain and should not be crossed in unstable early-season snow; steep sidehilling with real exposure starts once above treeline. The source text describes nothing above the start of the ramp.
